text: …thus attain awakening — all of them indeed abide here. Those that I am able to express in so many words — therefore accomplish them here. If you do not take delight in the Dharma of the Omniscient One, in later times you will surely come to regret it. However many perfections I have taught, and whatever paths of union with the ocean of gnosis — one whose bodily support abides in the conduct of the childish is not able to come to know them. When the times are evil and beings are wicked, at the end, when the Dharma wanes and the lower realms increase, the wise, having become utterly disillusioned, will grow heedful and fearful like deer. Supreme Delight King, compared with a bodhisattva who for a thousand eons, lacking skill in means, practices the six perfections, as against this heap of merit of one who, having heard this samādhi, rejoices in it, that former heap of merit does not approach even a hundredth part, and so on up to: it does not approach even a part expressible by comparison. When this Dharma discourse was taught, countless bodhisattvas generated the aspiration for unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening. All of them became irreversible from unsurpassed, perfect, complete awakening. Of the multitudes of gods and humans, some eight hundred thousand, too, free of dust and stainless,
